entries.name: claude-ask
entries.for: The example hosted worker the questions module's answering process asks Claude through (ADR 32, 33, 35): it streams the Messages API's answer to the task's output as it arrives, and completes the task with the whole answer. The API key is a header the kernel adds; the worker never sees it.

grants.policy: permit(principal == Worker::"claude-ask", action == Action::"work", resource == TaskType::"claude.ask");
grants.why: to work claude.ask tasks

grants.policy: permit(principal == User::"<you>", action == Action::"install", resource == TaskType::"claude.ask");
grants.why: to install it hosted, for whoever does (or be one of the server's BIZKERNEL_ADMINS)

grants.policy: permit(principal == Worker::"claude-ask", action == Action::"use", resource == Secret::"questions/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY");
grants.why: to call the Messages API with the key the kernel adds

hosted: echo 'permit(principal == Worker::"claude-ask", action == Action::"work", resource == TaskType::"claude.ask");' | bk policy add -
echo 'permit(principal == Worker::"claude-ask", action == Action::"use", resource == Secret::"questions/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY");' | bk policy add -

entries.name: file-intake
entries.for: The example self-hosted intake (ADR 71): follows a local file, each new line applied as its module's command, and continues where it stopped.
entries.follows: a file on this machine, each new line a JSON object applied as the command it is given

grants.policy: permit(principal == Worker::"file-intake", action == Action::"apply", resource in Module::"<the module whose command it applies>");
grants.why: to apply the commands it is given with what it reads

self_hosted: (cd cli && cargo build --release -p file-intake)
echo 'permit(principal == Worker::"file-intake", action == Action::"apply", resource in Module::"<the module whose command it applies>");' | bk policy add -
bk worker token create worker:file-intake   # an administrator: prints its token once
export BK_URL=<where the kernel listens> BK_TOKEN=<the token it printed>
cli/target/release/file-intake <file> <command>

entries.name: im-transcribe
entries.for: The worker the im module's transcribing process transcribes voice messages through (ADR 31, 79): run on the person's own Mac, it decodes a voice by its content type (WeChat's SILK) and hears it with SenseVoice-Small through sherpa-onnx, loaded when it starts, answering the text, the model and its version.

grants.policy: permit(principal == Worker::"im-transcribe", action == Action::"work", resource == TaskType::"voice.transcribe");
grants.why: to work voice.transcribe tasks

machine: sherpa-onnx 1.13.2's shared libraries, loaded when it starts: its macOS release sherpa-onnx-v1.13.2-osx-universal2-shared unpacked into ~/.cache/sherpa-onnx/dist, or SHERPA_ONNX_LIB_DIR set to its lib directory; another release is refused

the SenseVoice-Small model, sherpa-onnx-sense-voice-zh-en-ja-ko-yue-2024-07-17, in ~/.cache/sherpa-onnx, ~/.cache/modelscope or ~/.cache/huggingface/hub, or IM_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL set to its directory; it never downloads it

self_hosted: (cd cli && cargo build --release -p im-transcribe)
echo 'permit(principal == Worker::"im-transcribe", action == Action::"work", resource == TaskType::"voice.transcribe");' | bk policy add -
bk worker token create worker:im-transcribe   # an administrator: prints its token once
export BK_URL=<where the kernel listens> BK_TOKEN=<the token it printed>
cli/target/release/im-transcribe

entries.follows: an MQTT broker's topics, as its config (--config) names them and the command each message is applied as

grants.why: to sign in to the broker with the password its config names

hosted: echo 'permit(principal == Worker::"mqtt-intake", action == Action::"apply", resource in Module::"<the module whose command it applies>");' | bk policy add -

bk worker install mqtt-intake --allow-connect <broker host>:<port> --secret <module>/MQTT_PASSWORD --config <config.json>   # one of the server's BIZKERNEL_ADMINS
